predecessors.name: Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Britain, Gaul and Spain as the Roman Empire held them in 382: 'ruled Britain, Gaul, and Spain'

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Britain, Gaul, Spain and, from 387, Italy: after the Battle of Poetovio in 388 Valentinian II 'ruled from Gaul after being restored to power in 388' and Theodosius I held the East

ledger.x: 383: Magnus Maximus is proclaimed emperor in Britain.
25 August 383: Gratian is killed at Lyon and Gaul passes to Maximus.
387: Maximus invades Italy and Valentinian II flees.
June 388: Theodosius I marches west against Maximus.
August 388: Maximus surrenders at Aquileia and is executed.
28 August 388: Maximus is dead and his domain ends.

wars.name: Campaign of Theodosius I against Magnus Maximus (Battle of Poetovio)
wars.outcome: Theodosius I defeated Maximus at the Battle of Poetovio in 388; Maximus surrendered at Aquileia and was executed on 28 August 388, and Valentinian II was restored in Gaul.

certainty.note: The realm is named by provinces, never by boundaries: whether Hispania was held and how much of Italy are the pages' vague statements.
